question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

As we found previously, the slope is $m=3.$

Substituting $m=3$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=3x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(1,-4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x+b \\ -4 & =3(1)+b \\ -4 & =3+b \\ -7 & =b \\ b & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=3x-7.
$$

The coordinates of $B$ are $(3,2).$

* Since the vertical line should pass through $(3,2)$, the $x$-value for every point on the line is $3.$ Hence, the equation of that line is 

$$

* Since the horizontal line should pass through $(3,2)$, the $y$-value for every point on the line is $2.$ Hence, the equation of that line is 

$$
y=2.

From the picture, the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(1,-4)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(3,2),$ respectively.

To find the length of $\overset{―}{AB},$ we use the distance formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{―}{AB}| & =\sqrt{({x}_{2}-{x}_{1})^{2}+({y}_{2}-{y}_{1})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-1)^{2}+(2-(-4))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+36} \\  & =\sqrt{40} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

As we found previously, the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(1,-4)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(3,2),$ respectively.

Therefore, we compute the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-4-2}{1-3} \\  & =\frac{-6}{-2} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
